prompt: How is MCIT computed and when does it apply?
answer:
### Issue Presented
How is the Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT) computed and when does it apply?

### Short Answer
The Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT) is computed at a rate of 2% of the gross income as of the end of the taxable year, applicable starting from the fourth taxable year following the year in which the corporation commenced its business operations, provided that the MCIT exceeds the regular corporate income tax for that year.

### Controlling Authorities
- **RR No. 9-1998**: This regulation provides further details on the implementation of the MCIT.

### Legal Interpretation

### Practical Application
Corporations should monitor their income tax liabilities closely, especially as they approach the fourth year of operations. If the MCIT exceeds the regular corporate income tax, the corporation will be liable to pay the MCIT instead. Additionally, any excess MCIT paid can be carried forward and credited against the normal income tax for the next three taxable years. This provision allows corporations to manage their tax liabilities effectively, particularly in the early years of operation when profits may be lower.
